plain: Serious talk or writing on a subject

webster.text: The act of the understanding, by which it passes from premises to consequences; the act which connects propositions, and deduces conclusions from them.

more.text: Literally, a running over a subject in speech; hence, a communication of thoughts by words, either to individuals, to companies, or to public assemblies.

To communicate thoughts or ideas in a formal manner; to treat upon in a solemn, set manner; as, to discourse on the properties of the circle; the preacher discoursed on the nature and effects of faith.
To reason; to pass from premises to consequences.

example.quote: I presume that vague discourses and mere sports of fancy, not relative to the subject at all, are very improper on this interesting occasion.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 11, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
